extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark of 20,000 self-contradictory instructions across language-language and vision-language paradigms to evaluate large multimodal models' ability to detect conflicting commands.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, starting from manually input seeds and using generator, decorator, and cleaner stages, with quality checks by human experts and LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Manually input seeds, generated language/vision data, and ImageNet for SemanticConflict.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For vision-language conflicts, image captions and numerical data were modified to introduce contradictions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A cleaner removed data that did not meet quality standards, and the resulting dataset was refined to extract new seeds after quality checks by human experts and LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts and LLMs double-checked dataset quality, and human experts manually selected SCI-Base and SCI-Core subsets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper compares LLM-based evaluation with human expert evaluation using Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to help assess and improve LMMs' handling of conflicting instructions, promote inclusivity in AI research, and foster trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark currently only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, lacks fine-grained control over conflict degree, and does not provide a detailed study of attention mechanisms under conflicting instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models on detecting self-contradictory instructions.

isLiveDataset.evidence: We introduce the Self-Contradictory Instructions benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: SCI is constructed using our novel automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate (Fig. 3), which builds a multimodal cycle based on programs and large language models.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs).

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For V-L conflicts, the image caption is modified to introduce a conflict.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Here, the Generator creates initial language/vision data, the Decorator creates self-contradictions in the generated data, and the Cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate are calculated to measure the evaluation consistency between humans and LLM.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Our work on the SCI benchmark, along with the AutoCreate framework and CaP approach, has significant social implications.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: To begin with, we only include language-language and vision-language paradigms.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Hence, we propose a multimodal benchmark, Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI), to evaluate the ability of LMMs to detect conflicted instructions4.
